open_questions.question: Outside a flow, who may take a completed task into review: any agent other than its author (operator, 2026-10-26, option A).
Tasks closed as already built: approved once their evidence is accepted (operator, 2026-10-26, option A); at slice D's Fast level they close at once.

problem:
Four times in four days, rules that are each sensible combined into a task nobody could move:
- 2026-10-25, task 0759b1 (retrospective src-17aeb9aea81f, section 2.7): the mender re-recorded evidence and so became the author; the author may not move its task to review (403), QA could not move a task the mender held, completed -> approved is not an edge (409), and mend_reset_task refused. 20 runs passed it back and forth. Since then 996c85d lets the mender hand it to a reviewer, which works around this one case at the cost of a mender turn.
- 2026-10-24, task 5d4cf0a5006d (src-cb168bd3373f): outside a flow, the Architect was the named reviewer of DeveloperOpus's completed task. update_task(under_review) returned 403 because the author holds it; update_task(approved) returned 409. Only the operator could move it. In a flow the same hand-off works because the flow's review turn claims the task (task_transitions.py, BAND_AWAITING_HANDOFF: 'anybody else can'); direct delegation has no such path.
- 2026-10-23 (src-28d4bff83265): three specs approved after their work was built created 13 pending tasks for work already on master. A run takes at most one task, pending can only go to assigned or in_progress, no agent tool deletes a task, so closing them costs one paid run each, or the operator deleting them by hand (which they did on 2026-10-26).
- 2026-10-26, task-dadec899cc91 (the spec-page mock): landing it took the operator five attempts and the Architect three investigations. (1) The board offered 'Move to Under review', which was refused because the holder was the author. (2) Land was refused as 'commits on neither master nor inside any commit the accepted evidence names; ask the task's author to record evidence' while the evidence that would clear it already existed, awaiting a decision. (3) After the operator accepted it, Land was refused the same way: the evidence was for FR-11 and FR-12, added to the document after the task was created and never linked to it, and task_integration._targets counts only evidence reached through TaskRequirementLink. Linking them (update_task requirement_ids) cleared it; nothing said so. (4) Land then waited on checks that had restarted for the new tip; the drawer offered 'Land anyway', whose button is disabled until a reason is typed but does not look disabled, so pressing it did nothing. (5) Nothing said when the checks would finish; they are reported below the Notes section, with no estimate and no notice. Accept itself is reached only through the requirements chip's 'Show details' on the document.
The rule that the builder never approves is checked in about 16 places across 7 files (task_transition_service, scheduler, run_task_binding, agent_trigger, task_transitions, checkpoints), each answering a slightly different question, which is how the combinations above went unnoticed.
Also twice: list_evidence and record_evidence answer 404 'no specification document' for a spdoc- id that read_spec_document accepts (api/v1/agent_actions.py:1560, :1704).

requirements.rationale: Each dead end so far came from rules checked one at a time; only a test over the whole table catches the combination before an agent meets it.
requirements.statement: For every non-terminal task status and every kind of holder (none, the author, another agent, the mender), at least one agent can move the task to another status with the tools it is offered, except `blocked`, whose mover is the operator.

requirements.rationale: A state reserved for the operator is a dead end if the operator cannot see it.
requirements.statement: Every task whose only mover is the operator appears on the operator's Overview as waiting on them, with the action that moves it.

requirements.rationale: This is the hand-off a flow's review turn already makes (BAND_AWAITING_HANDOFF: 'not by the agent that finished it ... anybody else can'), and what slice D's Reviewed level means; one rule everywhere, and no named reviewer who can be busy or gone (operator, 2026-10-26).
requirements.statement: Outside a flow, any agent other than the one recorded as completing a task can move that completed task to under_review, and becomes its holder; the author still cannot.
The agent recorded as completing a task, including a mender that re-recorded its evidence, cannot move it to under_review or approve it.

requirements.rationale: Specs approved after interactive work shipped otherwise cost one paid run per task, or a flow started on them rebuilds shipped work. Roadmap slice C offers this at approval when intake recorded the work as already built.
requirements.statement: The operator can close every open task of an approved spec document in one action, naming the commit or commits on main that already hold the work, and no agent run is started for those tasks.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'already built' is checked like any other work, so the record stays trustworthy; on 2026-10-23 the check found a possible gap (the Composer's spinning send button). One review covers the whole document.
requirements.statement: Closing tasks as already built records, for each requirement those tasks serve, evidence pointing at the named commits, awaiting a decision like any other evidence; each task becomes approved only once the evidence for its requirements is accepted, and the action and its commits appear in each task's history.
list_evidence and record_evidence accept a document's spdoc- id wherever they accept its path, and answer the same as for the path.

requirements.rationale: The dead ends came from separate checks each answering a slightly different question; one answer is what lets slice D add levels and a lead without new dead ends.
requirements.statement: Every path that moves a task (update_task, a flow's staffing and review turn, the mender's tools, approval, the operator's board) gives the same answer, allowed or refused with the same reason, for the same status, holder and actor.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-26: the board offered 'Move to Under review', which keeps the author as holder and so can only be refused. A menu that offers a refused move teaches the operator that the menu cannot be trusted.
requirements.statement: From the board, the operator can move a completed task into review by choosing any agent other than its author, who becomes its holder; the board's status menu offers no move the Hub would refuse the operator.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-26: FR-11 and FR-12 were added to the spec-page document after its mock task existed; their evidence, recorded on that task from its checkout and accepted, merged nothing, because only evidence for linked requirements counts (task_integration._targets joins TaskRequirementLink). A document that grows while its task is open is normal in exploring and amending.
requirements.statement: Evidence recorded on a task against a requirement of that task's own spec document counts toward what approving the task merges, whether or not the requirement was linked to the task when the task was created.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-26: two refusals told the operator to ask the author for new evidence when the cause was evidence awaiting a decision and then a missing link, and 'Land anyway' was offered for checks that had not failed but were still running. A refusal that names the wrong remedy costs more than one that names none.
requirements.statement: When approving or landing a task is refused, the refusal names each cause the Hub can see and, in the operator's app, offers the action that clears it beside the refusal: Accept or Reject on each piece of evidence still awaiting a decision that approval would merge; linking a requirement whose accepted evidence on the task's branch the task does not serve; and, while the project's checks are still running on the work, a wait (with no override offered) instead of a refusal.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-26: the operator could not tell when the checks would finish (shown below the Notes, no estimate, no notice), and pressed a 'Land anyway' button that was disabled without looking it, so nothing happened.
requirements.statement: While approval of a task waits on its project checks, the task's Land control shows that it is waiting, for how long the checks have run and how long the previous run on that task took, and becomes available without a reload when they pass; when they finish the operator is notified; a control that cannot act looks disabled and says why.

in_scope: One decision of who may move which task, consulted by every path that moves one
A test over that decision: every unfinished status and holder situation has an actor able to move it
Outside a flow: any agent other than the author taking a completed task into review
From the board: the operator handing a completed task to a reviewer they name, and the board offering no move it would refuse
Closing all open tasks of a spec document whose work is already built, in one step, approved once their evidence is accepted
Evidence a task records against a requirement of its own document counting toward what approving that task merges
A refused approval or landing naming its cause and offering the action that clears it, including Accept on waiting evidence and the wait on running checks
spdoc- ids accepted wherever the evidence tools take a document
non_goals: Gate levels, a lead, reviewer pools and builders lists: roadmap slice D, which adds them as inputs to the decision built here (including closing already-built tasks at once at the Fast level)
Letting an author review or approve its own work: the rule that author and reviewer differ stays (slice D's Fast level is where it becomes a choice)
A reviewer field on create_task: any agent but the author may review (operator, 2026-10-26)
Judging each piece of evidence separately in a verdict: roadmap slice K
An assignee field on update_task: the operator still owns who holds a task, apart from the review hand-off this document adds
A blocked task (waiting on a person) gaining an agent mover: it is meant to wait for the operator, and must only be visible to them

Redesigning where evidence is judged on the spec page (the evidence chip on each requirement card): roadmap slice F, the spec-page wiring; this document only puts Accept beside a refusal that waits on it
Making checks faster or optional: the checks stay as they are; this document only makes their wait visible

summary: No task may sit in a state that nobody can move with the tools they are offered. Who may move which task becomes one decision, answered the same by every path that moves a task, so roadmap slice D can later add gate levels and a lead as new inputs to it rather than as more scattered checks. A test enumerates every unfinished status and holder against that decision and fails where there is no mover; the dead ends recorded on 23-26 October are removed: any agent other than the author can take a completed task into review outside a flow (and the operator can hand it to one from the board), a spec whose work is already built can have its open tasks closed in one step, waiting for one review of its evidence, and a refused landing names what clears it and offers it. The evidence tools also accept a document's spdoc- id, as read_spec_document does.

tasks.description: The acceptance drive first: write test_every_task_state_has_a_mover.py (the invariant and same-answer tests) and see it fail on master for completed/author outside a flow. Then bring the scattered who-may-move checks behind one decision that every moving path consults, and make it pass by letting any agent other than the author take a completed task into review outside a flow (becoming its holder), with author and mender-as-author still refused. Expose the decision's answer for the operator so the board can offer exactly it. Confirm blocked tasks are on the Overview with an action; fix if not.
